message.content:
Here’s a quick play‑by‑play guide you can follow right now—no coding required, but I’ll also show you how you could automate it later if you’re into scripting.

---

## 1️⃣ Pick a “nearby” theater

| Theater | Approx. distance from Times Square | Typical walk time |
|---------|-----------------------------------|-------------------|
| **AMC Empire 25** | ~0.4 mi (≈8 min) | 8–10 min |
| **Regal Union Square** | ~0.7 mi (≈12 min) | 12–15 min |
| **Alamo Drafthouse Cinema** | ~1.0 mi (≈18 min) | 18–20 min |
| **Cinemark 18 & XD** | ~1.2 mi (≈22 min) | 22–25 min |

> *Tip:* All of these are listed on Google Maps under “movie theaters near Times Square.” You can open the map, click on each theater, and the app will even give you walking directions and estimated travel time.

---

## 2️⃣ Check the showtimes

### Option A – Go straight to the theater’s own site

| Theater | Website |
|---------|---------|
| AMC Empire 25 | <https://www.amctheatres.com/movie-theaters/new-york-city/amc-empire-25> |
| Regal Union Square | <https://www.regmovies.com/theater/regal-union-square> |
| Alamo Drafthouse | <https://www.alamodrafthouse.com/cinema/alamo-drafthouse-cinema-new-york> |
| Cinemark 18 & XD | <https://www.cinemark.com/movies/cinemark-18-xd> |

*What to look for:*  
- Most sites let you filter by “Showtime” or “Movie Title.”  
- Once you pick a film, the page usually lists the runtime (e.g., “Runtime: 115 min”).  
- If the runtime isn’t shown, you can quickly look up the title on IMDb or TMDb (see below).

### Option B – Use a third‑party aggregator

| Aggregator | How to use |
|------------|------------|
| **Fandango** | <https://www.fandango.com/> → Search “Times Square, NY” → Pick a theater → Browse showtimes. |
| **Google Movies** | In Google Search, type “Movies near me” → Click “Showtimes” → Choose a theater. |
| **Flixster** | <https://flixster.com/> → Same process. |

These aggregators often display the runtime directly next to the showtime, so you can eyeball whether it’s ≤ 120 minutes.

---

## 3️⃣ Filter by runtime

If you’re doing this manually:

1. Pick a theater.  
2. Browse the list of films for the day.  
3. Look at the runtime column (or click the film title to see details).  
4. Keep only those with a runtime ≤ 120 minutes.

If you’d rather automate it, here’s a skeleton you can run locally (you’ll need a free TMDb API key; sign up at <https://developers.themoviedb.org/3/getting-started/introduction>):

```python
import requests

TMDB_API_KEY = "YOUR_TMDB_KEY"

def get_movie_runtime(movie_title):
    # Search for the movie ID first
    search_url = f"https://api.themoviedb.org/3/search/movie?api_key={TMDB_API_KEY}&query={movie_title}"
    r = requests.get(search_url)
    data = r.json()
    if not data["results"]:
        return None
    movie_id = data["results"][0]["id"]

    # Get detailed info
    detail_url = f"https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/{movie_id}?api_key={TMDB_API_KEY}"
    r = requests.get(detail_url)
    movie_info = r.json()
    return movie_info.get("runtime")  # returns runtime in minutes

# Example usage:
print(get_movie_runtime("Spider-Man: No Way Home"))  # → 148
```

Once you have the runtime, you can cross‑reference it against the showtimes you pulled from the theater’s site or an aggregator.

---

## 4️⃣ Quick sanity check

| Film | Runtime | Showtimes (example) | Recommendation |
|------|---------|---------------------|----------------|
| **The Batman** | 122 min | 7:30 pm, 9:45 pm | Slightly over 2 hrs – skip if strict. |
| **Knives Out** | 99 min | 6:00 pm, 8:30 pm | ✔️ Fits the 2‑hour rule. |
| **Soul** | 101 min | 5:45 pm, 8:15 pm | ✔️ |
| **The French Dispatch** | 106 min | 7:00 pm, 9:30 pm | ✔️ |

*(Numbers above are illustrative; always double‑check the actual showtimes on the theater’s site.)*

---

## Bottom line

1. **Pick a theater** (AMC Empire 25 is the closest).  
2. **Open its website** or use Fandango/Google Movies.  
3. **Look for the runtime** next to each film.  
4. **Choose a film ≤ 120 min** and book online or at the box office.

Happy watching! 🎬
